original_question: Which pro-inflammatory cytokine, known to be elevated in periodontal disease, is encoded by a gene that is located on chromosome 7 and is comprised of 5 exons?

final_qi.question: Which pro-inflammatory cytokine, known to be elevated in periodontal disease, is encoded by a gene that is located on chromosome 7 and is comprised of 5 exons?
final_qi.long_answer: The pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) is consistently found at elevated levels in periodontal disease. The human IL6 gene is situated on chromosome 7p15-p21 and is organized into 5 exons separated by 4 introns, matching the genomic description in the question.
